reasons.why: Listen addresses from configuration are overridden to port 8080 with environment variables (they take precedence over appsettings.json).
Windows paths in configuration (drive letters, UNC shares) are overridden with environment variables to folders under /data, which the manifests mount as volumes; the application code is not changed.
Targets net6.0, which is out of support: it runs on its own .NET 6.0 runtime image (no longer patched), as built and tested, not rolled forward onto a newer runtime.

ASP.NET Core Data Protection keeps its key ring under the user's home folder. The generated manifests mount one key there, read-only, from a Secret that External Secrets Operator generates once in the cluster, so every replica and restart shares it (PersistKeysTo* in code takes over when present).
The app logs to files under its own folder; the folder is made writable so start-up does not fail on the read-only root file system (console logging is preferred).

A dependency built for netstandard1.x pins System.* 4.0.x packages (SSH.NET 2016.x directly; Microsoft.Azure.Amqp 2.5.6 through System.Net.WebSockets.Client 4.0.2, pulled in by Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus 7.5.0 and MassTransit.Azure.ServiceBus.Core 7.3). Restoring for the linux-x64 runtime identifier adds runtime.unix.* packages that need 4.3.0, which NuGet reports as a package downgrade (NU1605, an error in SDK builds). A portable publish (no -r) restores the same graph as the Windows build and runs on the Linux runtime image. Upgrading the package (SSH.NET 2020.0.0+, a current Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus) removes the conflict.
